label: copy phase of long sequences, fed-back token 3/1/d (early recall)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L): zero activations in the original phase and at the <DEL> step, and only on copy-phase inputs (in_first is always 0). Strongly favors long sequences (L=9 holds 68% of mass, L=8 24%, L<=5 almost none) and early recall positions (recall_idx 2-3, i.e. the 2nd/3rd fed-back token, hold ~70% of mass; recall_idx 8 is a smaller secondary bump). Within this context it is token-selective: the fed-back input 3 (8x lift), 1 and d (5-6x) dominate, with weaker preference for q, x, 2, y, c, and output tokens x/3/c/t; rate also rises with the number of digits in the original sequence. Top activations are inputs of 3 at recall_idx 1-2 in long, digit-heavy sequences (e.g. 3 3 3 3 c j b b). Magnitude is largest at early recall positions with input 3. The predicate copy-phase & L>=8 & input in {3,1,d} gets only ~0.26 precision / 0.49 recall: the neuron behaves like a graded, token-weighted and position-weighted code rather than a clean binary condition, so the description is incomplete.
